## <a id="noura_plugin_types_0_1_0"></a>Import interface noura:plugin/types@0.1.0

What a capability interface returns when it refuses or fails a call.

----

### Types

#### <a id="property_error"></a>`record property-error`

A property whose value doesn't fit its object type's schema.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="property_error.property"></a>`property`: `string`
  <p>The property's name.

- <a id="property_error.code"></a>`code`: `string`
  <p>What is wrong, as the workspace format's validation codes say:
  `wrong_type`, `not_allowed`, `invalid_date` or `invalid_reference`.


#### <a id="error"></a>`variant error`



##### Variant Cases

- <a id="error.capability_not_declared"></a>`capability-not-declared`: `string`
  <p>The plugin doesn't hold the capability this call needs: its manifest
  doesn't declare it, or you revoked it. Holds the capability's name,
  such as `workspace-read`. The host ran nothing for the call. A write
  to an object whose type the plugin didn't register, a note for one,
  returns this too, naming `object-types`: the capability covers the
  plugin's own types only.

- <a id="error.unsupported_path"></a>`unsupported-path`
  <p>A file or folder name that a WIT string can't hold, such as one that
  isn't valid UTF-8. Noura never passes a changed copy of a name.

- <a id="error.invalid_path"></a>`invalid-path`: `string`
  <p>The path isn't a workspace-relative path with `/` between its parts:
  it is empty, absolute, holds `.`, `..` or `\`, or names a folder
  Noura keeps to itself, such as `.noura`. Holds the path.

- <a id="error.not_found"></a>`not-found`: `string`
  <p>Nothing in the workspace has this path or ID. Holds the path or ID.

- <a id="error.failed"></a>`failed`: `string`
  <p>The host couldn't finish the call. Holds a message for the plugin's
  author.

- <a id="error.network_refused"></a>`network-refused`: `string`
  <p>Noura refused a network request before connecting: the URL isn't
  HTTPS, its host or a redirect's host isn't one the plugin may reach,
  or the host is a local or private address. Holds the reason.

- <a id="error.target_not_declared"></a>`target-not-declared`: `string`
  <p>The manifest's `commands` capability doesn't name this command, or
  its plugin, among its targets. Holds the target, as
  `plugin/command`.

- <a id="error.target_unavailable"></a>`target-unavailable`: `string`
  <p>The target plugin isn't running in this workspace, or doesn't offer
  that command to other plugins. Holds the target, as
  `plugin/command`.

- <a id="error.busy"></a>`busy`: `string`
  <p>The target plugin is busy: the call would come back into a plugin
  that is waiting for this one, or the target stayed busy with another
  call. Holds the target plugin's ID.

- <a id="error.revision_conflict"></a>`revision-conflict`: `string`
  <p>The object's file changed since the plugin read it: it no longer
  holds the content revision the write carried. Nothing was written.
  Holds the object's ID.

- <a id="error.identity_conflict"></a>`identity-conflict`: `string`
  <p>More than one file holds this stable ID, as after a copy in another
  app, so writes by ID stop until only one file does. Holds the ID.

- <a id="error.invalid_property"></a>`invalid-property`: [`property-error`](#property_error)
  <p>A property doesn't fit the object type's schema. Nothing was
  written.

- <a id="error.already_exists"></a>`already-exists`: `string`
  <p>Something already has the path the write asked for. Holds the path.

## <a id="noura_plugin_objects_0_1_0"></a>Import interface noura:plugin/objects@0.1.0

Objects of the types the plugin registered: Markdown files in the
workspace with a stable ID, properties its schema checks, and a body.
Needs the `object-types` capability. A call about any other type, a
note for one, returns `capability-not-declared("object-types")` and
reaches no file. Writes carry the content revision the plugin read,
and return once the file is durably on disk. Chats and their messages,
which the AI plugin registers, change only through the `ai` interface:
`create`, `update`, `move-to` and `delete` return `failed` for them and
reach no file, while `get` and `list` read them.

redirects, each to a host the manifest lists. It refuses a URL that
isn't HTTPS, any other host, and a local or private address with

## <a id="noura_plugin_ai_0_1_0"></a>Import interface noura:plugin/ai@0.1.0

Chats with the AI providers you set up in Settings. Needs the `ai`
capability. Providers, their keys and your consent stay on this device,
and no call returns a key. Before a request carries this workspace's
content to a provider, Noura asks you in a prompt of its own whether
that provider may receive it, and it asks again after you change the
provider's kind, endpoint or model.

A chat is a folder of Markdown files in the workspace, `chat.md` and one
file per message, in the workspace format's chat layout. Noura writes
them, and each write is on disk before the call that made it returns.

Each request starts with Noura's instructions for the model, followed
by the body of the workspace's `AGENTS.md` when it has one. When a
chat's messages no longer fit the provider's context window, Noura
first asks the provider to summarize the earlier ones, writes the
summary to the chat as a context summary, and from then on sends the
summary in their place. Their files stay in the chat.

`web-search` and `web-fetch` let the model search the web with Brave
Search and read pages. Noura sends each request for the plugin, so the
plugin opens no connection of its own. They work once you add your
Brave Search key in Settings and allow web search for the workspace in
Noura's own prompt, which is a separate choice from a provider's
consent. Noura asks nothing per call.

Noura sends a search or a page read only to answer the model. One of
the plugin's runs must have completed with a call to the `web_search`
tool whose `query` argument matches, or to `web_fetch` whose `url`
argument matches, and still wait for `answer-tools`. Any other call
fails with `web_call_not_requested`, and nothing leaves the device.

----

  <p>A JSON Schema, as JSON text, for the tool's arguments.


#### <a id="tool_call"></a>`record tool-call`

A tool call the model asked for.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="tool_call.id"></a>`id`: `string`
  <p>The model's ID for the call, which the call's result names.

- <a id="tool_call.name"></a>`name`: `string`
- <a id="tool_call.arguments"></a>`arguments`: `string`
  <p>The arguments, as JSON text.


#### <a id="tool_result"></a>`record tool-result`

A tool's answer to a call, for the model.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="tool_result.call_id"></a>`call-id`: `string`
  <p>The ID of the call it answers.

- <a id="tool_result.name"></a>`name`: `string`
- <a id="tool_result.content"></a>`content`: `string`
  <p>The answer, as JSON text.


#### <a id="request"></a>`record request`

A message you wrote in a chat, for a provider to answer.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="request.chat"></a>`chat`: `string`
  <p>The chat's ID.

- <a id="request.provider"></a>`provider`: `string`
  <p>The provider's ID.

- <a id="request.message"></a>`message`: `string`
  <p>What you wrote, in Markdown.

- <a id="request.tools"></a>`tools`: list<[`tool-definition`](#tool_definition)>
  <p>The tools the model may ask to call.


#### <a id="run_status"></a>`enum run-status`



##### Enum Cases

- <a id="run_status.waiting_for_consent"></a>`waiting-for-consent`
  <p>Noura is asking you whether the provider may receive this
  workspace's content. Nothing is written or sent yet.

- <a id="run_status.denied"></a>`denied`
  <p>You said no. Nothing was written or sent.

- <a id="run_status.streaming"></a>`streaming`
  <p>The answer is streaming in.

- <a id="run_status.completed"></a>`completed`
  <p>The answer is complete. When the model asked for tools,
  `tool-calls` lists them.

- <a id="run_status.cancelled"></a>`cancelled`
  <p>You stopped it, or revoked the provider's consent. The answer so
  far stays in the chat as a cancelled message.

- <a id="run_status.failed"></a>`failed`
  <p>The provider or Noura failed. `failure` says why.

- <a id="run_status.waiting_for_approval"></a>`waiting-for-approval`
  <p>Noura is asking you whether to run one of the run's tool calls,
  after `run-tools`.

- <a id="run_status.interrupted"></a>`interrupted`
  <p>A plugin the run relied on was turned off: the plugin that sent it,
  or one whose tools it offered. Its failure's code is
  `plugin-disabled`, and the answer so far stays in the chat as an
  interrupted message.


#### <a id="failure"></a>`record failure`

Why a run failed, in public words. It never holds the provider's own
answer, its headers or a key.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="failure.code"></a>`code`: `string`
  <p>A stable code, such as `provider_request_failed`.

- <a id="failure.message"></a>`message`: `string`

#### <a id="run"></a>`record run`

A message you sent and its answer, as it streams in.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="run.id"></a>`id`: `string`
- <a id="run.chat"></a>`chat`: `string`
- <a id="run.provider"></a>`provider`: `string`
- <a id="run.status"></a>`status`: [`run-status`](#run_status)
- <a id="run.text"></a>`text`: `string`
  <p>The answer so far, in Markdown.

- <a id="run.message"></a>`message`: option<`string`>
  <p>The ID of the assistant message the answer goes to, once Noura wrote
  it.

- <a id="run.message_written"></a>`message-written`: `bool`
  <p>Whether Noura wrote your message to the chat. A run you denied or
  stopped while it waited, or one that failed before the write, leaves
  your message unwritten, so the plugin can give it back to you.

- <a id="run.tool_calls"></a>`tool-calls`: list<[`tool-call`](#tool_call)>
- <a id="run.failure"></a>`failure`: option<[`failure`](#failure)>

#### <a id="web_result"></a>`record web-result`

A page a web search found.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="web_result.title"></a>`title`: `string`
- <a id="web_result.url"></a>`url`: `string`
  <p>The page's `https` address.

- <a id="web_result.snippet"></a>`snippet`: `string`
  <p>The lines of the page Brave Search shows, as plain text.


#### <a id="web_page"></a>`record web-page`

A web page, as text.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="web_page.url"></a>`url`: `string`
  <p>The `https` address that answered, after any redirects.

- <a id="web_page.content_type"></a>`content-type`: `string`
  <p>The page's media type: `text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`,
  `text/plain` or `text/markdown`.

- <a id="web_page.text"></a>`text`: `string`
  <p>The page's text. An HTML page loses its markup, keeps emphasis as
  Markdown does and lists its links as numbered footnotes.

- <a id="web_page.truncated"></a>`truncated`: `bool`
  <p>Whether Noura cut the text at its size limit.


#### <a id="web_error"></a>`variant web-error`

Why a web search or a page read failed.

##### Variant Cases

- <a id="web_error.refused"></a>`refused`: [`error`](#error)
  <p>Noura refused the call as it refuses this interface's other calls,
  such as `capability-not-declared` with `ai` for a plugin that
  doesn't hold it.

- <a id="web_error.failed"></a>`failed`: [`failure`](#failure)
  <p>Noura or the web refused or failed. The code says why, such as
  `web_search_key_missing`, `web_consent_required`,
  `web_call_not_requested`, `web_search_key_rejected`,
  `web_search_rate_limited`, `web_url_not_https` or
  `web_url_unsafe_host`. The failure never holds the key or what
  Brave Search or the site answered.


----

### Functions

#### <a id="providers"></a>`providers: func`

The providers you set up and turned on.

##### Return values

- <a id="providers.0"></a> result<list<[`provider`](#provider)>, [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="chats"></a>`chats: func`

The workspace's chats, the one changed last first.

##### Return values

- <a id="chats.0"></a> result<list<[`chat`](#chat)>, [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="read_chat"></a>`read-chat: func`

A chat and its messages, oldest first. An answer or a tool call that
a crash or a quit left in progress, with no run of this session
behind it, reads as interrupted, and Noura writes it so: a tool call
reads as completed only when the chat holds its result, from the
same run, with the same call ID and tool name. Noura never runs such
a call again by itself.

##### Params

- <a id="read_chat.id"></a>`id`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="read_chat.0"></a> result<([`chat`](#chat), list<[`message`](#message)>), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="create_chat"></a>`create-chat: func`

Start a chat, titled `New chat` until its first message names it.
Noura writes the chat's files once its first message goes out, so a
chat whose first message you don't let go out leaves no file. Until
then `read-chat` shows it with no messages, and `chats` doesn't list
it.

##### Return values

- <a id="create_chat.0"></a> result<[`chat`](#chat), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="rename_chat"></a>`rename-chat: func`

Give the chat a new title. Fails with `revision-conflict` when its
`chat.md` no longer holds `expected-revision`, as after an edit in
another app, and then writes nothing.

##### Params

- <a id="rename_chat.id"></a>`id`: `string`
- <a id="rename_chat.title"></a>`title`: `string`
- <a id="rename_chat.expected_revision"></a>`expected-revision`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="rename_chat.0"></a> result<[`chat`](#chat), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="set_retention"></a>`set-retention: func`

Keep the chat until you delete it, or have Noura move it to the
trash 30 days after it started. Fails with `revision-conflict` as
`rename-chat` does.

##### Params

- <a id="set_retention.id"></a>`id`: `string`
- <a id="set_retention.retention"></a>`retention`: [`retention`](#retention)
- <a id="set_retention.expected_revision"></a>`expected-revision`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="set_retention.0"></a> result<[`chat`](#chat), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="workspace_tools"></a>`workspace-tools: func`

The tools that the plugins on in this workspace register under their
`tools` capability, for a request to offer the model. Each is named
`<plugin>__<tool>`, such as `tasks__create`.

##### Return values

- <a id="workspace_tools.0"></a> result<list<[`tool-definition`](#tool_definition)>, [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="send"></a>`send: func`

Send `request`. Noura writes your message and an in-progress answer to
the chat before the request leaves this computer, then the answer
streams in: `read-run` shows it so far, and Noura draws the plugin's views
again as text arrives. The answer and its status are on disk before
the run shows as completed, cancelled or failed. The first message of
a chat titled `New chat` gives the chat its title. Without your
consent for this workspace and provider, the run waits while Noura
asks you. A chat answers one message at a time.

##### Params

- <a id="send.request"></a>`request`: [`request`](#request)

##### Return values

- <a id="send.0"></a> result<[`run`](#run), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="answer_tools"></a>`answer-tools: func`

Answer the tool calls of a completed run with `results`, one per call,
and stream the model's next answer into the same run. Noura wrote each
call to the chat as in progress before the run showed as completed,
and it writes each result and completes its call before the next
request leaves this computer. `tools` are the tools the model may ask
to call next.

##### Params

- <a id="answer_tools.run"></a>`run`: `string`
- <a id="answer_tools.results"></a>`results`: list<[`tool-result`](#tool_result)>
- <a id="answer_tools.tools"></a>`tools`: list<[`tool-definition`](#tool_definition)>

##### Return values

- <a id="answer_tools.0"></a> result<[`run`](#run), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="run_tools"></a>`run-tools: func`

Run the tool calls of a completed run that name workspace tools, one
at a time, then stream the model's next answer into the same run.
For each call Noura asks you, in a prompt of its own that names the
tool, its plugin and its input, and runs the call in that plugin only
if you allow that one call. Meanwhile the run is
`waiting-for-approval`. Each call's result goes to the chat after the
call: the tool's answer, `{"denied":true}` when you deny the call or
close the prompt, or an `error` object. Stop, or opening another
workspace, denies the calls still waiting and ends the run. The next
request offers the tools the run offered whose plugins are still on.

##### Params

- <a id="run_tools.run"></a>`run`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="run_tools.0"></a> result<[`run`](#run), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="resume"></a>`resume: func`

Answer the chat's last message of yours again, as after a crash or a
quit stopped its answer, with `provider` and `tools`. Noura writes no
new message of yours, and asks for your consent as `send` does.

##### Params

- <a id="resume.chat"></a>`chat`: `string`
- <a id="resume.provider"></a>`provider`: `string`
- <a id="resume.tools"></a>`tools`: list<[`tool-definition`](#tool_definition)>

##### Return values

- <a id="resume.0"></a> result<[`run`](#run), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="read_run"></a>`read-run: func`

The run with this ID, as it stands now. `read-run`, `stop` and
`answer-tools` reach only the plugin's own runs: another plugin's run
is `not-found`.

##### Params

- <a id="read_run.id"></a>`id`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="read_run.0"></a> result<[`run`](#run), [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="stop"></a>`stop: func`

Stop a run. The provider request ends, and the answer so far stays as
a cancelled message.

##### Params

- <a id="stop.id"></a>`id`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="stop.0"></a> result<_, [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="web_ready"></a>`web-ready: func`

Whether the model may search the web and read pages in this
workspace: you added a Brave Search key and allowed web search for the
workspace. Offer the model web tools only then.

##### Return values

- <a id="web_ready.0"></a> result<`bool`, [`error`](#error)>

#### <a id="web_search"></a>`web-search: func`

Search the web with Brave Search for `query`, for at most
`max-results` results, from 1 to 10. Without a limit Noura asks for
10. Noura leaves out results without an `https` address. The query
must be one the model asked for in a `web_search` call.

##### Params

- <a id="web_search.query"></a>`query`: `string`
- <a id="web_search.max_results"></a>`max-results`: option<`u32`>

##### Return values

- <a id="web_search.0"></a> result<list<[`web-result`](#web_result)>, [`web-error`](#web_error)>

#### <a id="web_fetch"></a>`web-fetch: func`

Read the page at `url`, an `https` address on a public host that the
model asked for in a `web_fetch` call. Noura follows up to three
redirects, checks every address each host resolves to, and refuses a
local or private address before it connects. It reads only HTML and
plain text, up to 5 MiB, and cuts the text at 1 MiB. It gives up on a
page after 15 seconds, turning it into text included, and refuses a
page whose elements nest more than 1,024 deep. The time spent waiting
doesn't count toward the call's deadline.

##### Params

- <a id="web_fetch.url"></a>`url`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="web_fetch.0"></a> result<[`web-page`](#web_page), [`web-error`](#web_error)>

## <a id="noura_plugin_ui_0_1_0"></a>Import interface noura:plugin/ui@0.1.0

UI as data. WIT has no recursive types, so a view is a flat list of nodes
whose `children` hold indices into the list. The first node is the root.

Every label must hold more than spaces: Noura reads it to screen readers.

----

### Types

#### <a id="item"></a>`record item`

A line in a list: a label and an optional quieter detail after it, on
the same line. A board's card shows the detail under the label.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="item.label"></a>`label`: `string`
- <a id="item.detail"></a>`detail`: option<`string`>
- <a id="item.checked"></a>`checked`: option<`bool`>
  <p>A checkbox before the label, checked or not, which you check or
  uncheck by click or the space bar. Each change sends `checked`, and
  the box then shows what the plugin draws. Only list and virtual
  list items show one: a card holding one breaks the rules.

- <a id="item.warning"></a>`warning`: option<`string`>
  <p>A short warning after the label, such as `Overdue`, in the color
  Noura shows problems in. Screen readers read it with the label.
  Only list and virtual list items show one.


#### <a id="item_list"></a>`record item-list`

A list you select items in.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="item_list.label"></a>`label`: `string`
  <p>Names the list for screen readers.

- <a id="item_list.reorder"></a>`reorder`: `bool`
  <p>Whether you can drag its items to new positions. A drop sends
  `moved`, and the list then shows the items in the order the plugin
  draws them.

- <a id="item_list.selected"></a>`selected`: option<`string`>
  <p>The node ID of the item the list shows selected, such as the view
  you're in. When the plugin draws another one than it drew before,
  or none, the list's selection moves there; otherwise the item you
  selected last stays selected.

- <a id="item_list.opens_on_click"></a>`opens-on-click`: `bool`
  <p>Whether one click opens an item, as a link does: a click sends
  `selected` when the item wasn't selected, then `activated`. The
  arrow keys still only select. Enter and a double-click open an item
  in every list.


#### <a id="name_field"></a>`record name-field`

A one-line field that names something: a new task, or a rename. It
takes the keyboard each time it appears, holding `value`. Enter, or
leaving the field, sends `named` with what it holds, and Escape sends
`cancelled`, as does leaving it empty or holding the name it started
from. A name still in the field when its window closes is sent first,
even one sent before that the plugin kept in the field, as after a
create that failed.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="name_field.label"></a>`label`: `string`
  <p>Names the field for screen readers, and shows in it while it's
  empty.

- <a id="name_field.value"></a>`value`: `string`
  <p>The name the field starts from: empty for something new, the
  current name for a rename.


#### <a id="virtual_list"></a>`record virtual-list`

A list of items fetched as they scroll into view, so it can hold more
rows than a view holds nodes. Noura calls the view's `rows` for them.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="virtual_list.label"></a>`label`: `string`
  <p>Names the list for screen readers.

- <a id="virtual_list.rows"></a>`rows`: `u32`
  <p>How many rows the list holds, at most 1,000,000.


#### <a id="virtual_row"></a>`record virtual-row`

One row of a virtual list, as `rows` returns it.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="virtual_row.id"></a>`id`: `string`
  <p>Unique within the list. Events name the row by this ID.

- <a id="virtual_row.item"></a>`item`: [`item`](#item)

#### <a id="sort_order"></a>`enum sort-order`



##### Enum Cases

- <a id="sort_order.ascending"></a>`ascending`
- <a id="sort_order.descending"></a>`descending`

#### <a id="column"></a>`record column`

A table's column.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="column.id"></a>`id`: `string`
  <p>Unique within the table. A header press names the column by it.

- <a id="column.title"></a>`title`: `string`
  <p>The header's text.

- <a id="column.sorted"></a>`sorted`: option<[`sort-order`](#sort_order)>
  <p>Shows that the table is sorted by this column, and in which order.


#### <a id="table"></a>`record table`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="table.label"></a>`label`: `string`
  <p>Names the table for screen readers.

- <a id="table.columns"></a>`columns`: list<[`column`](#column)>

#### <a id="form"></a>`record form`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="form.label"></a>`label`: `string`
  <p>Names the form for screen readers.

- <a id="form.submit"></a>`submit`: `string`
  <p>The label of the button that submits the form.

- <a id="form.required"></a>`required`: list<`string`>
  <p>The node IDs of text inputs inside the form that must hold more
  than spaces before you can submit it. The submit button shows
  disabled until they do.


#### <a id="value"></a>`variant value`

What an input holds. The case sets the kind of input Noura draws.

##### Variant Cases

- <a id="value.text"></a>`text`: `string`
  <p>A single line of text.

- <a id="value.multiline"></a>`multiline`: `string`
  <p>Several lines of text.

- <a id="value.checkbox"></a>`checkbox`: `bool`
- <a id="value.choice"></a>`choice`: option<`string`>
  <p>The ID of the chosen option, or none.

- <a id="value.date"></a>`date`: option<`string`>
  <p>A date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, the workspace format's date, or none.

- <a id="value.date_time"></a>`date-time`: option<`string`>
  <p>A date and time in RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, such as
  `2026-10-21T09:30:00-04:00`, or none.


#### <a id="choice"></a>`record choice`

One option of a single-choice input.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="choice.id"></a>`id`: `string`
  <p>Unique within the input. The input's value names the option by it.

- <a id="choice.label"></a>`label`: `string`

#### <a id="input"></a>`record input`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="input.label"></a>`label`: `string`
- <a id="input.value"></a>`value`: [`value`](#value)
- <a id="input.choices"></a>`choices`: list<[`choice`](#choice)>
  <p>The options of a choice input. Other inputs have none.


#### <a id="menu_item"></a>`record menu-item`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="menu_item.label"></a>`label`: `string`
- <a id="menu_item.enabled"></a>`enabled`: `bool`
  <p>A disabled item shows but can't be chosen.


#### <a id="calendar_mode"></a>`enum calendar-mode`

The period a calendar grid shows.

##### Enum Cases

- <a id="calendar_mode.month"></a>`month`
  <p>Six weeks from the Sunday on or before the first of the month.

- <a id="calendar_mode.week"></a>`week`
  <p>Sunday to Saturday, with a row of all-day entries above the hours.

- <a id="calendar_mode.day"></a>`day`
  <p>One day, with a row of all-day entries above the hours.


#### <a id="calendar"></a>`record calendar`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="calendar.label"></a>`label`: `string`
  <p>Names the grid for screen readers.

- <a id="calendar.mode"></a>`mode`: [`calendar-mode`](#calendar_mode)
- <a id="calendar.date"></a>`date`: `string`
  <p>A day of the period to show, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.


#### <a id="calendar_entry"></a>`record calendar-entry`

A dated entry in a calendar grid. Noura draws it on each day it
covers, in this device's time zone.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="calendar_entry.title"></a>`title`: `string`
- <a id="calendar_entry.start"></a>`start`: `string`
  <p>An all-day entry's first day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or a timed entry's
  start in RFC 3339 with an offset.

- <a id="calendar_entry.end"></a>`end`: option<`string`>
  <p>The end, in the form of the start: the day after an all-day
  entry's last day, or a timed entry's end. Without an end, or with
  one not after the start, an all-day entry takes its first day and a
  timed entry 30 minutes.


#### <a id="node_kind"></a>`variant node-kind`



##### Variant Cases

- <a id="node_kind.panel"></a>`panel`: option<`string`>
  <p>Lays out its children from top to bottom. The label names the panel
  for screen readers.

- <a id="node_kind.text"></a>`text`: `string`
  <p>A line of plain text.

- <a id="node_kind.markdown"></a>`markdown`: `string`
  <p>Markdown, drawn by Noura. Images show as their description and never
  load from the network.

- <a id="node_kind.button"></a>`button`: `string`
  <p>A button with this label. Presses come back by the node's ID. A
  button whose child is a menu opens the menu instead.

- <a id="node_kind.list"></a>`list`: [`item-list`](#item_list)
  <p>A list you select items in, by click or arrow keys. Its children
  are its items.

- <a id="node_kind.item"></a>`item`: [`item`](#item)
  <p>An item of a list. Its only child may be a menu, which opens by
  right-click or from the keyboard, or a name field, which shows in
  the item's place, as for a rename.

- <a id="node_kind.virtual_list"></a>`virtual-list`: [`virtual-list`](#virtual_list)
  <p>A list whose rows come from the view's `rows`. It holds no children.

- <a id="node_kind.table"></a>`table`: [`table`](#table)
  <p>A table. Its children are its rows.

- <a id="node_kind.row"></a>`row`: list<`string`>
  <p>A table row: one cell per column, at least one of them with text.
  Screen readers name the row by its first cell with text. Its only
  child may be a menu.

- <a id="node_kind.form"></a>`form`: [`form`](#form)
  <p>Lays out its children like a panel, with a submit button after them.
  Submitting, by the button or Enter in a single-line text input
  inside it, sends the value of every input inside it.

- <a id="node_kind.input"></a>`input`: [`input`](#input)
  <p>A labeled input. Changes come back by the node's ID.

- <a id="node_kind.name_field"></a>`name-field`: [`name-field`](#name_field)
  <p>A field that names something, which goes where an input goes or
  in a list item's place. What you name comes back by the node's ID.

- <a id="node_kind.menu"></a>`menu`: `string`
  <p>A menu with this label, the child of an item, a row, a card or a
  button. Its children are menu items and separators, at least one
  item among them.

- <a id="node_kind.menu_item"></a>`menu-item`: [`menu-item`](#menu_item)
  <p>A menu item. Choosing it sends its node ID.

- <a id="node_kind.separator"></a>`separator`
  <p>A line between menu items.

- <a id="node_kind.board"></a>`board`: `string`
  <p>A board, named for screen readers by this label. Its children are
  its columns, at least one. You drag cards within a column and
  between the board's columns: a drop sends `moved`, and the board
  then shows the cards where the plugin draws them, so a move the
  plugin refuses puts the card back.

- <a id="node_kind.board_column"></a>`board-column`: `string`
  <p>A column of a board, with this label in its header. Its children
  are its cards.

- <a id="node_kind.card"></a>`card`: [`item`](#item)
  <p>A card in a board column, with its detail under its label. You
  select a card by click or arrow keys and open it by double-click or
  Enter, which send `selected` and `activated` naming the board. Its
  only child may be a menu, which opens by right-click or from the
  keyboard.

- <a id="node_kind.calendar"></a>`calendar`: [`calendar`](#calendar)
  <p>A calendar grid of the period the record sets. Its children are its
  entries; it draws those in the period. Its mode and period change
  only when the plugin draws new ones, such as after a press of one
  of its own buttons.

- <a id="node_kind.entry"></a>`entry`: [`calendar-entry`](#calendar_entry)
  <p>An entry of a calendar grid. You select an entry by click or the
  keyboard and open it by double-click or Enter, which send `selected`
  and `activated` naming the calendar.


#### <a id="node"></a>`record node`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="node.id"></a>`id`: `string`
  <p>Unique within the view. Events name the node by this ID.

- <a id="node.kind"></a>`kind`: [`node-kind`](#node_kind)
- <a id="node.children"></a>`children`: list<`u32`>
  <p>Indices into the view's node list. Panels and forms hold the nodes
  they lay out, lists their items, tables their rows, boards their
  columns, columns their cards, calendars their entries, and menus
  their items; a row, a card or a button may hold one menu, and an
  item one menu or one name field.


#### <a id="target"></a>`record target`

An item of a list, a row of a table, a card of a board or an entry
of a calendar grid.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="target.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The node ID of the list, virtual list, table, board or calendar.

- <a id="target.item"></a>`item`: `string`
  <p>The item's, the row's, the card's or the entry's node ID, or a
  virtual list row's ID.


#### <a id="move"></a>`record move`

A card or a list item dragged to a new place. Nothing moves until the
plugin draws it there.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="move.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The node ID of the board or the list.

- <a id="move.item"></a>`item`: `string`
  <p>The node ID of the card or the item.

- <a id="move.to"></a>`to`: `string`
  <p>The node ID of the column the card was dropped in, or the list's
  own node ID.

- <a id="move.position"></a>`position`: `u32`
  <p>Where it goes among that column's cards or the list's items,
  counted from 0 as if it had already left its old place.


#### <a id="column_press"></a>`record column-press`

A header press in a table.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="column_press.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The table's node ID.

- <a id="column_press.column"></a>`column`: `string`
  <p>The column's ID.


#### <a id="field"></a>`record field`

An input's value.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="field.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The input's node ID.

- <a id="field.value"></a>`value`: [`value`](#value)

#### <a id="submission"></a>`record submission`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="submission.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The form's node ID.

- <a id="submission.fields"></a>`fields`: list<[`field`](#field)>
  <p>Every input inside the form, in view order.


#### <a id="check"></a>`record check`

An item's checkbox, checked or unchecked.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="check.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The node ID of the list or the virtual list.

- <a id="check.item"></a>`item`: `string`
  <p>The item's node ID, or a virtual list row's ID.

- <a id="check.checked"></a>`checked`: `bool`
  <p>Whether the box is checked now.


#### <a id="naming"></a>`record naming`

A name typed in a name field.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="naming.node"></a>`node`: `string`
  <p>The name field's node ID.

- <a id="naming.name"></a>`name`: `string`
  <p>The name, without spaces at either end. It holds more than spaces
  and differs from the name the field started from.


#### <a id="event"></a>`variant event`

Something you did in a view.

##### Variant Cases

- <a id="event.pressed"></a>`pressed`: `string`
  <p>The button with this node ID was pressed.

- <a id="event.selected"></a>`selected`: [`target`](#target)
  <p>An item, a row, a card or an entry was selected, by click or the
  keyboard.

- <a id="event.activated"></a>`activated`: [`target`](#target)
  <p>An item, a row, a card or an entry was opened, by double-click or
  Enter.

- <a id="event.sorted"></a>`sorted`: [`column-press`](#column_press)
  <p>A table's column header was pressed, so the plugin can sort.

- <a id="event.changed"></a>`changed`: [`field`](#field)
  <p>An input's value changed.

- <a id="event.submitted"></a>`submitted`: [`submission`](#submission)
  <p>A form was submitted.

- <a id="event.chosen"></a>`chosen`: `string`
  <p>The menu item with this node ID was chosen.

- <a id="event.moved"></a>`moved`: [`move`](#move)
  <p>A card or a list item was dropped in a new place.

- <a id="event.checked"></a>`checked`: [`check`](#check)
  <p>An item's checkbox was checked or unchecked.

- <a id="event.named"></a>`named`: [`naming`](#naming)
  <p>A name field holds a new name: you pressed Enter in it or left it,
  or its window closed.

- <a id="event.cancelled"></a>`cancelled`: `string`
  <p>A name field was left without a new name: you pressed Escape, or
  left it empty or holding the name it started from. Holds the
  field's node ID.

### Functions

#### <a id="pages"></a>`pages: func`

The pages the plugin adds to the rail.

##### Return values

#### <a id="render"></a>`render: func`

The nodes of a page's view.

##### Params

- <a id="render.page"></a>`page`: `string`

##### Return values

#### <a id="sidebar"></a>`sidebar: func`

The nodes of the section a page adds to the sidebar, above the file
tree, while the page shows: none for no section. The section can't
hold a virtual list, and its node IDs don't repeat the page view's.

##### Params

- <a id="sidebar.page"></a>`page`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="sidebar.0"></a> list<[`node`](#node)>

#### <a id="rows"></a>`rows: func`

Rows `start` up to `start + count` of the virtual list with node ID
`node` in a page's view, as they scroll into view. Return fewer when
the list ends sooner.

##### Params

- <a id="rows.page"></a>`page`: `string`
- <a id="rows.node"></a>`node`: `string`
- <a id="rows.start"></a>`start`: `u32`
- <a id="rows.count"></a>`count`: `u32`

##### Return values

- <a id="rows.0"></a> list<[`virtual-row`](#virtual_row)>

#### <a id="handle_event"></a>`handle-event: func`

Something happened in a page's view or its sidebar section. Noura
draws the plugin's views again afterwards.

##### Params

- <a id="handle_event.page"></a>`page`: `string`
- <a id="handle_event.event"></a>`event`: [`event`](#event)

## <a id="noura_plugin_commands_0_1_0"></a>Export interface noura:plugin/commands@0.1.0

----

### Types

#### <a id="command"></a>`record command`



##### Record Fields

- <a id="command.id"></a>`id`: `string`
  <p>Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, and
  unique within the plugin. Other plugins name it as
  `plugin/command` in their targets.

- <a id="command.title"></a>`title`: `string`
  <p>The name the command palette shows.

- <a id="command.palette"></a>`palette`: `bool`
  <p>Whether the command palette lists it.

- <a id="command.plugins"></a>`plugins`: `bool`
  <p>Whether other plugins that name it as a target may call it.


----

### Functions

#### <a id="commands"></a>`commands: func`

The commands the plugin offers.

##### Return values

- <a id="commands.0"></a> list<[`command`](#command)>

#### <a id="run"></a>`run: func`

Run the command `id`. From the command palette `input` is empty; from
another plugin it is what that plugin sent. The answer, or a message
that says why the command failed, goes back to the plugin that called.
Noura draws the plugin's views again afterwards.

##### Params

- <a id="run.id"></a>`id`: `string`
- <a id="run.input"></a>`input`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="run.0"></a> result<`string`, `string`>
